explanation_en: This expression is commonly used in legal, administrative, and professional contexts to indicate when a law, contract, or decision officially starts to apply. It is synonymous with 'entrer en vigueur' but is slightly more versatile, as it can also apply to personal agreements or changes in employment. Note that the verb 'prendre' is conjugated, while 'effet' remains singular.

examples.en_text: The new contract will take effect on January 1st.
examples.target_text: Le nouveau contrat prendra effet le 1er janvier.

examples.en_text: These new security measures take effect immediately.
examples.target_text: Ces nouvelles mesures de sécurité prennent effet immédiatement.

examples.en_text: My resignation took effect last week.
examples.target_text: Ma démission a pris effet la semaine dernière.

examples.en_text: The subscription would take effect after the trial period.
examples.target_text: L'abonnement prendrait effet après la période d'essai.

examples.en_text: I want this decision to take effect as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: Je souhaite que cette décision prenne effet le plus vite possible.

examples.en_text: The new law will only take effect after its official publication.
examples.target_text: La nouvelle loi ne prendra effet qu'après sa publication officielle.

explanation_en: This adverbial phrase means 'in two steps' or 'in two phases.' It is often used in business, politics, or project planning to describe a process that is not immediate but split into distinct parts. It can also be extended to 'en deux temps, trois mouvements' to mean 'in a jiffy' or 'very quickly,' though in this context it refers strictly to a two-step process.

examples.en_text: We are going to carry out this project in two stages: first the planning, then the creation.
examples.target_text: Nous allons réaliser ce projet en deux temps : d'abord la planification, puis la création.

examples.en_text: The meeting took place in two stages, with a coffee break in the middle.
examples.target_text: La réunion s'est déroulée en deux temps, avec une pause-café au milieu.

examples.en_text: The move was done in two stages to avoid too much stress.
examples.target_text: Le déménagement s'est fait en deux temps pour éviter trop de stress.

examples.en_text: The teacher explained this difficult rule in two stages so that everyone would understand.
examples.target_text: Le professeur a expliqué cette règle difficile en deux temps pour que tout le monde comprenne.

examples.en_text: Our communication strategy will be rolled out in two stages starting on Monday.
examples.target_text: Notre stratégie de communication va se déployer en deux temps à partir de lundi.

examples.en_text: His response came in two stages: first a short message, then a long explanatory email.
examples.target_text: Sa réponse est venue en deux temps : d'abord un message court, puis un long mail explicatif.

explanation_en: When followed by a time indicator, 'd'ici' means 'by' or 'between now and' a certain deadline. It is a crucial prepositional phrase for setting deadlines in both professional and casual French. Be careful not to confuse it with 'd'ici là,' which means 'by then' or 'in the meantime.'

examples.en_text: We absolutely must finish this project by the end of the week.
examples.target_text: Il faut absolument que nous terminions ce projet d'ici la fin de la semaine.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, your package should arrive by tomorrow noon.
examples.target_text: Ne t'inquiète pas, ton colis devrait arriver d'ici demain midi.

examples.en_text: A lot of things can change between now and then, so let's not make a decision too quickly.
examples.target_text: Beaucoup de choses peuvent changer d'ici là, alors ne prenons pas de décision trop vite.

examples.en_text: The doctor said I would feel much better within a few days.
examples.target_text: Le médecin a dit que je me sentirais beaucoup mieux d'ici quelques jours.

examples.en_text: I hope to receive my refund by next month.
examples.target_text: J'espère recevoir mon remboursement d'ici le mois prochain.

examples.en_text: If you have any questions, send me a message by this evening.
examples.target_text: Si tu as des questions, envoie-moi un message d'ici ce soir.

explanation_en: 'Une entrave' is a formal but common noun meaning a hindrance, obstacle, or shackle. Combined with the preposition 'à,' it is frequently used in political, legal, and journalistic debates to describe measures that restrict rights or progress. It collocates strongly with abstract nouns like 'la liberté,' 'le développement,' or 'la justice.'

examples.en_text: The lack of budget is an obstacle to the completion of our project.
examples.target_text: Le manque de budget est une entrave à la réalisation de notre projet.

examples.en_text: Her excessive shyness is sometimes an obstacle to her professional career.
examples.target_text: Sa timidité excessive est parfois une entrave à sa carrière professionnelle.

examples.en_text: These new administrative rules are an obstacle to innovation.
examples.target_text: Ces nouvelles règles administratives sont une entrave à l'innovation.

examples.en_text: The roadworks represent an obstacle to traffic this morning.
examples.target_text: Les travaux sur la route représentent une entrave à la circulation ce matin.

examples.en_text: A poor internet connection is a real obstacle to working from home.
examples.target_text: Une mauvaise connexion internet est une véritable entrave au télétravail.

examples.en_text: Water pollution is an obstacle to the development of tourism in the region.
examples.target_text: La pollution de l'eau est une entrave au développement du tourisme dans la région.

explanation_en: This common idiom means to be confronted with, to deal with, or to face someone or something. It is highly frequent in spoken and written French across all registers. A common spelling mistake even among native speakers is writing 'avoir à faire à' instead of 'avoir affaire à.'

examples.en_text: If you are not satisfied, you will have to deal with the director.
examples.target_text: Si vous n'êtes pas satisfait, vous aurez affaire au directeur.

examples.en_text: In this investigation, we are dealing with a very intelligent criminal.
examples.target_text: Dans cette enquête, nous avons affaire à un criminel très intelligent.

examples.en_text: If you hurt my sister again, you will have to deal with me.
examples.target_text: Si tu fais encore du mal à ma sœur, tu auras affaire à moi.

examples.en_text: I have already dealt with this administrative department and they are very slow.
examples.target_text: J'ai déjà eu affaire à ce service administratif et ils sont très lents.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, you are dealing with a very competent doctor.
examples.target_text: Ne t'inquiète pas, tu as affaire à un médecin très compétent.

examples.en_text: For this project, we are going to deal with serious competitors.
examples.target_text: Pour ce projet, nous allons avoir affaire à des concurrents sérieux.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to drag one's feet,' this idiomatic expression is used figuratively to describe someone who acts with reluctance, delays taking action, or stalls. It is common in everyday speech, political commentary, and workplace discussions. It is informal but perfectly acceptable in professional debates.

examples.en_text: The children are dragging their feet about going to bed tonight.
examples.target_text: Les enfants traînent les pieds pour aller au lit ce soir.

examples.en_text: The government is dragging its feet on voting for this new environmental law.
examples.target_text: Le gouvernement traîne les pieds pour voter cette nouvelle loi sur l'environnement.

examples.en_text: My brother is dragging his feet about selling his old car, even though he doesn't use it anymore.
examples.target_text: Mon frère traîne les pieds pour vendre sa vieille voiture, même s'il ne l'utilise plus.

examples.en_text: If the team keeps dragging their feet, we will never finish this project on time.
examples.target_text: Si l'équipe continue de traîner les pieds, nous ne finirons jamais ce projet à temps.

examples.en_text: Why are you dragging your feet about sending this registration form?
examples.target_text: Pourquoi est-ce que tu traînes les pieds pour envoyer ce formulaire d'inscription ?

examples.en_text: I had to insist that she come to the party; she really dragged her feet.
examples.target_text: J'ai dû insister pour qu'elle vienne à la fête, elle a vraiment traîné les pieds.

explanation_en: This is one of the most essential idiomatic verbs in French, meaning 'to realize' or 'to become aware of.' It is pronominal and always followed by 'que' (with the indicative) or 'de' (with a noun/infinitive). A common pitfall is using 'réaliser' in this sense, which is an anglicism, although increasingly accepted; 'se rendre compte' remains the most natural and correct choice.

examples.en_text: They realize that the project is more difficult than expected.
examples.target_text: Ils se rendent compte que le projet est plus difficile que prévu.

examples.en_text: I realized that I had left my keys in the car.
examples.target_text: Je me suis rendu compte que j'avais oublié mes clés dans la voiture.

examples.en_text: You need to realize the importance of this decision.
examples.target_text: Tu dois te rendre compte de l'importance de cette décision.

examples.en_text: She didn't realize the danger at the time.
examples.target_text: Elle ne s'est pas rendu compte du danger sur le moment.

examples.en_text: When you get there, you will realize the beauty of the landscape.
examples.target_text: Quand tu seras sur place, tu te rendras compte de la beauté du paysage.

examples.en_text: Do you realize what you are saying?
examples.target_text: Est-ce que vous vous rendez compte de ce que vous dites ?

explanation_en: This colloquial expression literally means 'to hit to the side' and figuratively means 'to miss the mark,' 'to be off-target,' or 'to miss the point.' It is widely used in informal and semi-formal discussions to criticize an ineffective measure or an incorrect guess. It contrasts with 'taper dans le mille' (to hit the bullseye).

examples.en_text: You have good intentions, but I think you're missing the mark.
examples.target_text: Tu as une bonne intention, mais je pense que tu tapes à côté.

examples.en_text: Our last advertising campaign completely missed the mark.
examples.target_text: Notre dernière campagne publicitaire a complètement tapé à côté.

examples.en_text: Without the right numbers, we risk missing the mark.
examples.target_text: Sans les bons chiffres, on risque de taper à côté.

examples.en_text: My parents want to help me, but they often miss the mark.
examples.target_text: Mes parents veulent m'aider, mais ils tapent souvent à côté.

examples.en_text: I tried to guess her age, but I completely missed the mark.
examples.target_text: J'ai essayé de deviner son âge, mais j'ai complètement tapé à côté.

examples.en_text: Her analysis of the situation is interesting, but it misses the mark a bit.
examples.target_text: Son analyse de la situation est intéressante, mais elle tape un peu à côté.

explanation_en: The verb 's'empêtrer' (or the past participle 'empêtré') literally means to get caught or tangled (like a foot in a rope). Figuratively, it is widely used in political and business contexts to describe being stuck in a complex, difficult situation or scandal from which it is hard to extricate oneself. It carries a slightly negative or critical connotation.

examples.en_text: He is entangled in a complicated relationship that he doesn't know how to get out of.
examples.target_text: Il est empêtré dans une relation compliquée dont il ne sait pas comment se sortir.

examples.en_text: The company has been bogged down in financial problems since last year.
examples.target_text: L'entreprise est empêtrée dans des problèmes financiers depuis l'année dernière.

examples.en_text: By dint of lying, she got caught up in her own explanations.
examples.target_text: À force de mentir, elle s'est empêtrée dans ses propres explications.

examples.en_text: The bill is bogged down in endless political debates.
examples.target_text: Le projet de loi est empêtré dans des débats politiques sans fin.

examples.en_text: I got bogged down in the technical details and lost precious time.
examples.target_text: Je me suis empêtré dans les détails techniques et j'ai perdu un temps précieux.

examples.en_text: The mayor finds himself entangled in a corruption scandal.
examples.target_text: Le maire se retrouve empêtré dans un scandale de corruption.

explanation_en: Derived from the verb 'user' (to wear out/down), 'une guerre d'usure' is a common military and political collocation meaning a war of attrition. It is used metaphorically in everyday French to describe any long-term conflict, negotiation, or struggle where the goal is to slowly wear down the opponent's resolve or resources.

examples.en_text: The negotiations between the union and management turned into a real war of attrition.
examples.target_text: Les négociations entre le syndicat et la direction se sont transformées en une véritable guerre d'usure.

examples.en_text: This tennis match wasn't a question of technique, but rather a physical war of attrition.
examples.target_text: Ce match de tennis n'était pas une question de technique, mais plutôt une guerre d'usure physique.

examples.en_text: Between the two neighbors, it's a daily war of attrition to see who will get the best parking spot.
examples.target_text: Entre les deux voisins, c'est une guerre d'usure quotidienne pour savoir qui aura la meilleure place de parking.

examples.en_text: The two political parties are engaged in a war of attrition to wear out the opposition's voters.
examples.target_text: Les deux partis politiques se livrent une guerre d'usure pour lasser les électeurs de l'opposition.

examples.en_text: Facing this aggressive competitor, our strategy is to wage a war of attrition on prices.
examples.target_text: Face à ce concurrent agressif, notre stratégie est de mener une guerre d'usure sur les prix.

examples.en_text: I refuse to get into this psychological war of attrition with my boss.
examples.target_text: Je refuse d'entrer dans cette guerre d'usure psychologique avec mon patron.

explanation_en: This semi-auxiliary construction literally translates to 'to let hear,' but idiomatically means to suggest, imply, or hint at something without stating it directly. It is highly common in journalism and formal discussions to report on implicit stances or rumors. Note that it is often used with a neuter pronoun 'le' (e.g., 'comme le laissent entendre...').

examples.en_text: The latest press articles suggest that the minister will soon resign.
examples.target_text: Les derniers articles de presse laissent entendre que le ministre va bientôt démissionner.

examples.en_text: The dark clouds on the horizon suggest that a storm is approaching.
examples.target_text: Les nuages noirs à l'horizon laissent entendre qu'une tempête approche.

examples.en_text: His vague explanations imply that he is hiding something.
examples.target_text: Ses explications floues laissent entendre qu'il cache quelque chose.

examples.en_text: The company managers imply that there will be hiring soon.
examples.target_text: Les dirigeants de l'entreprise laissent entendre qu'il y aura des recrutements bientôt.

examples.en_text: Her colleagues imply that she is going to get a promotion.
examples.target_text: Ses collègues laissent entendre qu'elle va obtenir une promotion.

examples.en_text: The clues found on-site suggest that the culprit acted alone.
examples.target_text: Les indices trouvés sur place laissent entendre que le coupable a agi seul.

explanation_en: Originating from old French ('huis' meaning door), this fixed adverbial phrase means 'behind closed doors' or 'in private.' It is widely used in legal, political, and diplomatic contexts to describe meetings, trials, or negotiations that are closed to the public and press.

examples.en_text: The board of directors met behind closed doors to discuss the budget.
examples.target_text: Le comité de direction s'est réuni à huis clos pour discuter du budget.

examples.en_text: The trial took place behind closed doors to protect the identity of the witnesses.
examples.target_text: Le procès s'est déroulé à huis clos pour protéger l'identité des témoins.

examples.en_text: The two presidents spoke in private for more than two hours.
examples.target_text: Les deux présidents ont discuté à huis clos pendant plus de deux heures.

examples.en_text: Due to recent incidents, the next soccer match will be played behind closed doors.
examples.target_text: À cause des récents incidents, le prochain match de football se jouera à huis clos.

examples.en_text: I prefer that we settle this family issue in private, without the neighbors.
examples.target_text: Je préfère que nous réglions ce problème familial à huis clos, sans les voisins.

examples.en_text: The disciplinary hearing will be held behind closed doors this afternoon.
examples.target_text: Le conseil de discipline se tiendra à huis clos cet après-midi.
